subject: Re: Marketplace SKU bundle — channel fee pass-through & escalation
messages:
From: Julia Romano <julia.romano@acme-health.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme-health.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace bundle question: channel fee pass-through

Hi Chloe,

Quick question as we're assembling the PO for the pilot: for the composite SKU you proposed (bundle of inference + managed logging), can Redwood support a channel fee pass-through to our reseller?

Specifically: our reseller requires a 12% net pass-through on list price for marketplace private offers (AWS). Your pricing worksheet shows a single blended SKU — we'd need either

- a mechanistic pass-through (list price split) so the reseller sees their 12% on the invoice, or
- an equivalent uplift applied to the SKU so the settlement to Redwood is net of the reseller margin.

Can you confirm which approach Redwood supports for AWS private offers, and whether there are any restrictions on bundling multiple services into a single SKU for the marketplace?

Thanks — we want to finalize the purchase order by next week.

Best,
Julia Romano
Head of Procurement
Acme Health

[attachment: acme_po_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: Julia Romano <julia.romano@acme-health.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace bundle question: channel fee pass-through

Hi Julia — thanks for the clear note. Cutting to the answer: we can support both patterns, but each has tradeoffs from a channel and accounting perspective. High-level:

- Option A — List-price split (recommended when reseller needs explicit line-item visibility): create two SKUs in the private offer (bundle_base + reseller_fee) so the reseller's 12% is visible and flows through. This preserves clean channel reporting but requires marketplace SKU mapping and may increase listing complexity.

- Option B — Uplifted single SKU (simpler on the marketplace but opaque to reseller): inflate the bundle price so the reseller margin is absorbed in the list price. Simpler for PO creation but the reseller won't see a direct 12% line item on their invoice.

A few important constraints:
- AWS private offer tooling prefers stable SKU IDs; adding an extra SKU increases operational overhead for renewals.
- GCP marketplace has a stronger preference for single-product SKUs for billing reconciliation, so Option B is often easier there.
- Taxes and VAT handling: uplifted SKUs need to be modeled carefully so the reseller's taxable base doesn't get mis-stated.

I've attached a quick channel-split workbook illustrating both approaches and the net-to-Redwood impact at different usage tiers. Can you confirm which approach your reseller prefers? If they require visibility, we'll provision two SKUs and route settlement accordingly.

Next steps:
- If you confirm Option A, Ben will run a channel margin workback and provide revised SKU mapping (need reseller legal name and tax ID).
- If Option B, we'll update the PO amount and send a revised private offer.

Thanks,
Chloe Martin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com
615-555-0198

[attachment: proposed_channel_split_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, Julia Romano <julia.romano@acme-health.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Mar 2028 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace bundle question: channel fee pass-through

Julia / Chloe — looping in a quick margin view. I ran both models in the attached pricing_model_v2.xlsx and here are the caller-outs:

- If we do Option A (two SKUs):
  * Reseller gets explicit 12% on the reseller_fee SKU; Redwood receives net on the bundle_base SKU. After AWS marketplace fees and a small distributor handling fee (we typically reserve 1.5%), net to Redwood is ~83% of list across expected usage bands.
  * Upside: clean audit trail and reseller visibility. Downside: potential PRN mismatch on monthly usage reconciliation with AWS.

- If we do Option B (single uplifted SKU):
  * Simple purchase flow for Acme and fewer SKUs to maintain. Net to Redwood is similar after embedding the reseller margin into list price, but reseller doesn't have a separate line item which some procurement teams dislike.
  * Risk: marketplace invoicing templates differ across clouds — GCP especially may reclassify tax base.

Questions for Acme:
- Do you have a reseller legal entity and tax ID yet for the purchase? That will determine whether we can do a pass-through invoice.
- Which cloud are you planning to use for the private offer (AWS or GCP)? You indicated AWS in the PO preface — we can proceed there and test reconciliation.

I'll prepare a short channel margin memo for your finance team if you confirm Option A.

Ben
Director, Marketplace Sales
ben_carter@redwood.com
[attachment: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Julia Romano <julia.romano@acme-health.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, chloe_martin@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 9 Mar 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace bundle question: channel fee pass-through

Thanks for the detail, Ben and Chloe — this is helpful. Quick answers:

- Reseller: HealthDistribution LLC (EIN: 12-3456789). They require an explicit line item reflecting 12% of list price.
- Cloud: AWS private offer for this pilot.

We'd like to proceed with Option A (two SKUs) so the reseller sees the 12% on the invoice — visibility is a compliance requirement for our procurement. Can Redwood scope the operational handshake for monthly reconciliation? Specifically:

- Who at Redwood will own the monthly usage reconciliation with HealthDistribution?
- What reporting cadence and format can you provide (CSV with SKU-level usage + gross/list price + reseller_fee line)?
- Can you add a short clause to the PO/contract that clarifies reseller pass-through and settlement timing?

If you can send an updated SKU mapping and a short reconciliation template by next Wednesday (2028-03-15), we can route the PO to legal.

Appreciate the speed — looking forward to the channel memo.

Best,
Julia
